away.name: Joel Hofer
away.news: Jordan Binnington led the Blues to their first Stanley Cup in the 2018-19 season, but he has struggled to perform at a consistently high level. Last season, the Blues gave an increased workload to Joel Hofer, who eventually outplayed Binnington in the latter half of the season and earned more playing time. Building on that trend, the Blues turned to Hofer in their season opener, and he stopped all 25 shots he faced in a 4-0 win over the Dallas Stars, adding to his case for the team's starting goalie. The Blues enter Tuesday as -140 road favourites against a Chicago Blackhawks team that has been outscored 15-5 in its first three games (0-3-0).

away.name: Brandon Bussi
away.news: Bussi emerged out of nowhere last season as a 27-year-old making his NHL debut, playing admirably in the Hurricanes' crease and ultimately helping lead them to a Stanley Cup. He carried that momentum into the 2026-27 season, saving 19 of 20 shots (.950 SV%) in his season debut, a 1-0 overtime loss to the Florida Panthers. That said, he struggled in his following outing, allowing five goals on 27 shots (.815 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the Washington Capitals. The Hurricanes will likely alternate between Bussi and Pyotr Kochetkov this season, but they will start Bussi on Tuesday for the third time in four games. Carolina enters the action on Tuesday as -117 road favourites against the Montreal Canadiens, who have scored eight goals in their first two games (1-0-1).

home.name: Jakub Dobes
home.news: After a breakout 2025-26 season that continued into an impressive postseason run, Dobes has struggled early in the 2026-27 season. Through two games, the 25-year-old Czech goalie has allowed eight goals on 58 shots (.862 SV%) while posting a 1-0-1 record. Montreal's dominant offence has bailed Dobes out so far, but he will need to be better on Tuesday when he tends the twine against the Carolina Hurricanes. The Canadiens enter the action as slight +106 home underdogs.

away.name: Juuse Saros
away.news: Having not played since Saturday, the Predators were likely always turning to Saros to tend the twine on Tuesday, but Justus Annunen (undisclosed) surfacing on Injured Reserve sealed the deal. The 31-year-old Saros has had a solid start to the 2026-27 season, posting a 2.03 GAA and .933 SV% in two outings (1-1-0). He played exceptionally well in his previous game, saving 29 of 30 shots (.967 SV%) in a 2-1 win over the Dallas Stars. The Predators enter Tuesday's contest as +134 road underdogs against a Toronto Maple Leafs team that has scored just six goals through three games this season (1-2-0).

home.name: Anthony Stolarz
home.news: The Maple Leafs are off to a 1-2-0 start, but hope to return to .500 on Tuesday, turning to Stolarz to tend the twine against the Nashville Predators. The 32-year-old Stolarz battled injuries in 2025-26 and had a disappointing season, but he was stellar in his only outing of 2026-27 thus far, saving 26 of 27 shots (.963 SV%) in a 2-1 victory over the New York Islanders. The Maple Leafs enter Tuesday's contest as -148 home favourites against a Predators team coming off a 2-1 win over the Dallas Stars.

away.name: Karel Vejmelka
away.news: Vejmelka played a career-high 64 games last season and could be due for another busy season, with rookie Sebastian Cossa as his backup. The 30-year-old Vejmelka was perfect in his opening game, saving all 15 shots he faced in a 6-0 win over the Chicago Blackhawks, but struggled in his follow-up outing, allowing three goals on 18 shots (.857 SV%) in a 4-2 loss to the New York Rangers. The Mammoth enter Tuesday as slight +111 road underdogs against a New Jersey Devils team coming off an embarrassing 6-0 loss to the New York Islanders.

home.name: Jake Allen
home.news: After trading Jacob Markstrom in the offseason, the Devils are rolling with a makeshift goalie tandem of Jake Allen and Nico Daws. The 36-year-old Allen has started 35 or fewer games in six of his past seven seasons, so it's unclear if the team will rely on him more heavily in 2026-27, but he was stellar in his only outing so far, saving 23 of 25 shots (.920 SV%) in a 3-2 overtime victory over the Philadelphia Flyers. The Devils enter Tuesday as -122 home favourites against a Utah Mammoth team that has outscored its opposition 12-5 through games this season (2-1-0).

away.name: Semyon Varlamov
away.news: Varlamov has battled a myriad of injuries over the past two seasons, but will return to this crease on Tuesday for his first start since November 29th, 2024. The veteran 38-year-old goalie has put together an excellent career, posting a 2.65 GAA and .916 SV% in 621 career games (289-232-71). That said, in his most recent season, albeit a small sample size, Varlamov was pacing for one of the worst seasons of his career, posting a 2.89 GAA and .889 SV% in 10 appearances (3-4-3). The Islanders enter Tuesday's contest as +130 road underdogs against a New York Rangers team on a three-game winning streak.

home.name: Igor Shesterkin
home.news: Shesterkin was named the NHL's opening-week first star and will hope to build on that momentum heading into week two. The 30-year-old Russian goalie posted a stellar 1.67 GAA and .934 SV% in three games (2-1-0), capping it by scoring his first career goal into an empty net in a 5-1 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning. The Rangers enter Tuesday as -151 home favourites against a New York Islanders team coming off a dominant 6-0 win over the New Jersey Devils.

away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: With Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined to the start of the season, Minnesota will continue to rely on Wallstedt, turning to him for his third straight game to start 2026-27. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie has given Head Coach John Hynes no reason to deviate, posting a stellar 1.01 GAA and .957 SV% through two games (2-0-0). Minnesota enters the action on Tuesday as slight -106 road favourites against a Buffalo Sabres team that has been outscored 9-7 through two games (1-1-0).

home.name: Colten Ellis
home.news: Ellis is expected to start Tuesday vs. the Wild.
